problem: Exact global git HEAD equality is appropriate as a contemporaneous anti-replay invariant inside one WP14/promoter run, but it is too coarse as the sole durable equivalence identity in a high-churn monorepo: unrelated research/receipt commits can advance HEAD without changing ClayCode release inputs.

current_supported_invariant.reason: Prevents replaying an old coherent target bundle into a newer checkout during release mutation.

proposed_durable_identity.name: ReleaseInputClosureDigest
proposed_durable_identity.purpose: Distinguish release-relevant source/input changes from unrelated monorepo churn without weakening provenance.
minimum_fields: dependency/lock/config digests that affect lowering or execution
target/build environment fingerprint required by the acceptance contract
proposed_durable_identity.durable_freshness_rule: A later repository revision may reuse an accepted release epoch only if the complete declared release-input closure and required environment/toolchain identity remain cryptographically identical; any relevant-input change invalidates the epoch and requires re-execution.
proposed_durable_identity.authority_rule: Closure equality is evidence reuse eligibility, never execution/effect authority.

primary_external_support.relevant_mechanism: Build actions declare required inputs, commands/environment, and cache/reuse is keyed from action/input identity rather than arbitrary repository wall-clock churn.
Provenance tracks artifacts to source revision and supports cryptographic digests for source/content/material identity.
Content-addressing separates object identity from unrelated external metadata and motivates content-derived release identity.

strongest_counterhypothesis: Global git commit identity alone is simpler, complete and safer; path/input closure risks omitting hidden dependencies and producing false equivalence.
why_not_promoted_now: The complete transitive ClayCode release input closure has not yet been enumerated and measured.
An incomplete closure would be more dangerous than conservative exact-HEAD invalidation because it could silently reuse stale evidence.
Current BASE is not PASS, so correctness dominates avoiding future redundant reruns.

required_discriminating_tests_before_pro.intervention: Change only an unrelated research/receipt artifact outside the declared release input closure.
required_discriminating_tests_before_pro.expected: global git commit changes; release_input_closure_sha256 stays identical; durable release eligibility may remain valid.

required_discriminating_tests_before_pro.intervention: Change a compiler/runtime/acceptance source that can affect ClayCode output.
required_discriminating_tests_before_pro.expected: release_input_closure_sha256 changes and prior release epoch becomes stale.

required_discriminating_tests_before_pro.intervention: Change a relevant dependency lock, compiler/runtime version, lowering config or target ABI input.
required_discriminating_tests_before_pro.expected: closure/environment identity changes and prior release epoch becomes stale.

required_discriminating_tests_before_pro.intervention: Vary an undeclared input while all declared closure records remain constant.
required_discriminating_tests_before_pro.expected: If output/semantics change, candidate closure is REFUTED/INCOMPLETE until that dependency is captured.

required_discriminating_tests_before_pro.intervention: Attempt to reuse old target receipts after a release-input mutation.

promotion_gate: Do not replace or relax exact-HEAD contemporaneous checks until complete closure discovery plus the hidden-input falsifier passes on local, Hostinger-compatible and Andreas target evidence lanes where applicable.
rollback: No runtime change in this candidate; current exact-HEAD freshness checks remain authoritative.
